limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not determine whether complement-labelled and eliminated terminals are connected to WNV-infected or healthy neurons.
Astrocyte contribution to synapse elimination cannot be completely ruled out due to differing lysosomal digestion rates.
Alterations to NMDA receptor-mediated long-term potentiation could also contribute to altered synapse homeostasis and memory.
The study uses a single WNV mutant strain (NS5-E218A) and intracranial route; generalizability to natural peripheral infection and other neurotropic viruses is not established.
Human data are from a small number of post-mortem samples (n=5 WNV cases).

The causal chain from complement activation to microglial engulfment to memory impairment is inferred from separate experiments; direct in vivo demonstration of complement-dependent microglial phagocytosis causing memory deficits is not provided.
The study does not address whether complement-mediated synapse elimination prevents trans-synaptic viral spread.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

claims.statement: WNV-NS5-E218A intracranial infection in mice results in high survival (90%) with viral clearance by 15 dpi and low neuronal apoptosis, providing a recovery model.

experiments_or_tasks: Intracranial inoculation of 8-week-old C57BL/6J mice with 10^4 pfu WNV-NS5-E218A; survival monitored; viral brain burdens measured by plaque assay at 6-8 dpi and clearance by 15 dpi; neuroinflammation assessed by flow cytometry at 7 dpi; neuronal apoptosis quantified by TUNEL/NeuN at 7 dpi.

methods.name: Intracranial inoculation
